title: Finite assembly theorem and source-bound PR799 application
body:
Fixed backoffs and a fixed bootstrap depth leave a gap below the retained balanced assembly's supplied-cap ceiling. This PR adds a constructive finite-parameter theorem, an exact verifier, and source-bound applications to PR433 and PR799. The source-basis, contract-checking and E8 contributions below remain included.

### Finite assembly theorem

For admitted rational bit and complex caps `c,b`, put `a0 = 384599/10^10` and `u = min(b,c)`. Under `a0 < u`, `b < 1/32`, an admitted finite coefficient charge, and the inherited weighted-bootstrap and bridge premises, every rational

```text
0 < kappa < u/(1+u)
```

has a finite constructible witness. The constructor selects positive backoffs, finitely many bootstrap levels and explicit integer cutoffs, then checks all 47 retained strict inequalities. The proof establishes termination and the greatest admissible point on any supplied rational grid. This ceiling is relative to the supplied caps and this assembly family; the endpoint is never attained.

Start with the [proof](https://github.com/lydakis/integer-mult-bounds/blob/524375c61b75dc10cef68a71d504e79e7e7f138c/research/finite-assembly-frontier/PROOF.md), [constructor](https://github.com/lydakis/integer-mult-bounds/blob/524375c61b75dc10cef68a71d504e79e7e7f138c/research/finite-assembly-frontier/assembly.py) and [historical package](https://github.com/lydakis/integer-mult-bounds/tree/524375c61b75dc10cef68a71d504e79e7e7f138c/research/finite-assembly-frontier). The complete 51-file historical package is retained unchanged from `e819106`, including its PR433 fixture, five behavioral tests, source notices and receipts. It remains self-contained for default offline verification.

### Source-bound PR799 application

The [PR799 adapter](https://github.com/lydakis/integer-mult-bounds/tree/524375c61b75dc10cef68a71d504e79e7e7f138c/research/finite-assembly-pr799) applies that same theorem to the maintainer-admitted native-complex PR799 and unchanged PR589 bit supplier at upstream `f567884aeb8851b6e794af1184119a3bfbe1e631`.

| Conditional value | Kappa |
| --- | --- |
| Pinned PR799 baseline | `0.001661634653669567` |
| Finite witness on the `10^-27` grid | `0.001661634653669567075843432` |

The difference is only `7.5843432e-20`. The contribution is a reusable theorem and reproducible admission interface. This parameter improvement is not a substantive frontier advance, new supplier construction or practical speedup. As of 2026-10-13, open [PR890](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/890) reports `0.001661957774647029` in the same conditional integer model ([pinned claim](https://github.com/chafreaky/integer-mult-bounds/blob/4b3bd8cbe8e3e81c44161017c9b72c905a8040a8/research/complex-t21-owners/data/CLAIM.json)), above this application. No current numerical lead is claimed here; PR890 has not been independently replayed by this PR.

The adapter verifies 144 immutable upstream file bindings and the unchanged core package. It uses the original PR741/PR799 receipt checkers and admission code, binds the exact integrated replay's owner and invoice, reproduces the complete published assembly, and then constructs the new witness with nine finite levels. Both rational engines check the selected seed; all finite cutoffs and 47 strict inequalities pass. The next grid point and ceiling endpoint are rejected, as are zero eta, zero beta and unit beta.

Recurrence policy is explicit: native complex omits the bad-residue surcharge; bit retains it. Conservative admission runs first. The complex finite invoice is recomputed. The unchanged bit coefficient bound `393 < 512` and row bound `18355` are reused through the authenticated PR589 records; the underlying bit coefficient integer and physical suppliers are not rebuilt.

### Reproduction and validation

Historical example:

```sh
python3 -B research/finite-assembly-frontier/verify.py
```

Current application, after obtaining the pinned upstream snapshot using the [README commands](https://github.com/lydakis/integer-mult-bounds/blob/524375c61b75dc10cef68a71d504e79e7e7f138c/research/finite-assembly-pr799/README.md):

```sh
python3 -E -S -B research/finite-assembly-pr799/verify.py \
  --upstream ../integer-mult-pr799-upstream \
  --output ../integer-mult-pr799-result
```

The verifier runs offline with Python 3.11+ and the standard library. It records exact parameters, cutoffs, moment intervals, constraints and completion hashes. A local bounded validation reproduced the complete portable result and rejected three isolated source mutations before scientific imports: sibling README, upstream input and core input. Original inputs remained unchanged. Root independently checked the source bindings, execution receipts and exact rational result; Ody performed the bounded runs and independent workflow review.

Current head: [`524375c`](https://github.com/lydakis/integer-mult-bounds/commit/524375c61b75dc10cef68a71d504e79e7e7f138c). All 60 jobs passed across the five existing fork push workflows on this exact commit: [research/formal verification](https://github.com/lydakis/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/38392189883), [graded box convolution](https://github.com/lydakis/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/38392190153), [terminal elimination](https://github.com/lydakis/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/38392190102), [recycled bit registers](https://github.com/lydakis/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/38392189936) and [early reset/kernel composition](https://github.com/lydakis/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/38392189908). These existing workflows do not include a dedicated PR799 adapter job; the new adapter is covered by the bounded local validation described above. Upstream pull-request workflows separately report `action_required` without running jobs. Fork CI does not establish upstream approval.

### Scope and attribution

Supplier compiler, common-label/mutable-source realization, whole-call hosting, restored work, fixed tape/common grid, precision, weighted bootstrap and analytic/H1-H5 interfaces remain assumptions. This PR does not establish unconditional multiplication complexity, global optimality or a new Lean proof.

George Lydakis contributed the finite-assembly theorem and adapter with OpenAI Codex assistance, including Ody. Original licenses and cumulative notices remain authoritative. The application credits Jeremy Kothe's PR799, Chafik Boukhalfa's PR741 frames, DreamingOfClouds' PR589 on eumemic's PR555, Rohan Arun's PR559 correction, icekylinx and the earlier supplier, engine, owner and analytic-interface contributors. The historical package retains PR433 and its full upstream attribution.
